## Detailed entries

### Allen County

- **Type:** County
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** Ordinance 26-03 shows a handwritten second-reading date that appears to read May 24, 2026; this requires confirmation against fiscal court minutes. A June 10, 2026 WNKY article reports the ordinance had been adopted without dating the vote.
- **Normalized date:** `—` (unverified)
- **Duration:** 24 months (2 years)
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ky-allen-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Allen County Fiscal Court Ordinance No. 26-03
- **What prompted it:** Proactive measure; increased statewide data-center development interest and concerns about infrastructure, energy consumption, land use, and environmental sustainability; officials said existing regulations may not adequately address large-scale data facilities
- **Affected projects:** None identified; proactive measure ahead of any specific proposal
- **Detailed status:** Ordinance 26-03 imposes a two-year moratorium and says it takes effect immediately upon second reading and adoption. The handwritten second-reading date appears to read May 24, 2026, but requires corroboration; WNKY reported adoption on June 10 without specifying the vote date. The exact end and current force have not been established. Earlier reporting attributed neighboring counties’ use of the ordinance as a model.
- **Outcome:** Two-year moratorium on construction, development, and operation of data centers and data storage facilities adopted via Ordinance No. 26-03.

### Executive Order 2026-494 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `ky-executive-order-2026-494-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Governor Andy Beshear; —
- **Recorded status:** Governor-signed order dated August 6, 2026; official journal lists the padded number 2026-0494 as filed August 6, 2026, and the filed copy includes the attestation/seal and received-and-filed stamp. The order expressly states effectiveness August 6, 2026; subsequent legal force remains unverified.
- **Provisions:** Requires data-center developers to submit energy plans protecting residential ratepayers and assuring energy needs can be met now, in the near term and long term without additional costs to other utility ratepayers. Directs the Public Service Commission not to allow utilities to increase rates paid by other ratepayers to recover costs caused by data-center development and operation. Directs the Energy and Environment Cabinet to deny permit applications where a data center would negatively affect listed environmental resources and requires compliance with applicable environmental laws and public-engagement requirements. Requires tax and community-engagement commitments and preserves local-community decisions on data-center operations. The order does not establish a categorical moratorium or repeal all statutory incentives.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; mixed
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2026-08-06
- **End condition and limitations:** No express end date identified in the complete two-page order. Later amendment, rescission, judicial developments and actual project applicability remain unverified.
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://web.sos.ky.gov/execjournalimages/2026-MISC-2026-0494-301849.pdf>)

### HB 775 (2025 RS)

- **Policy ID:** `ky-hb-775-2025-rs`
- **Sponsor / party:** J. Nemes; R (KY House Republican)
- **Recorded status:** Became law without Governor's signature 2025-03-27 (Acts Ch. 98)
- **Provisions:** Amended KRS 154.20-220 to remove the prior 500,000-population consolidated-government location requirement and add county-population-based minimum investments for owners, operators and colocation tenants. The currently retrieved definition requires at least $450 million in counties with population at least 100,000, $100 million above 50,000 but below 100,000, or $25 million at 50,000 or below, using the specified ACS estimate at application; project organizers have a separate $150 million threshold. These minimum investments are due by the fifth anniversary of preliminary approval. This is statutory eligibility text, not a finding that an individual project qualifies.
